- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.6) and forecast spikes, reduce overshoot by 5–15% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.3) and forecast remains high, apply downward bias correction, especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 3–7% downward adjustment for days 1–10.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.3–0.6), model often overestimates mean; apply a 2–5% downward correction to align with recent 10–15 day average.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast decline by 10–20% in the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model underestimates downside risk — add 3–8% buffer to lower end of forecast range for 3–7 days.
- Forecast horizon 1–7 days: model often misses short-term mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- Forecast horizon 8–30 days: model tends to overestimate volatility — apply 2–5% smoothing to avoid overreacting to sentiment spikes.
